record.question:
Financial batches arrive in an encrypted S3 raw-data bucket. Only an approved processing role may read them, and raw records must never enter queues, job arguments, logs or the downstream bucket. A tested PySpark job masks account numbers, joins each batch to a large reference dataset and emits JSON in about 20 minutes. Catalog definitions already exist. The team must reuse this whole-batch code, meet a 60-minute target and avoid managing a compute cluster.

Which processing design meets these requirements?

options.text: Send each raw record through SQS to a Lambda consumer that masks it before writing downstream.
Run the unchanged Spark transformation in one standard Lambda invocation with a 30-minute timeout.

Start a Glue Spark job with object references when a complete batch is ready. Use the approved role and catalog metadata, validate the sanitized output in restricted staging, then publish the accepted batch downstream.
Run a Glue crawler to update the catalog and copy the raw objects downstream when the crawler succeeds.

explanation.text:
<<3>> is correct. A Glue Spark job can execute the existing transformation without operating a cluster. The catalog describes data; the job actually masks and reshapes it. A separate validation and publication gate prevents a failed or incomplete sanitization attempt from becoming a downstream batch.

<<1>> violates the explicit prohibition on placing raw records in queues. <<2>> exceeds the 15-minute limit of a standard Lambda invocation and does not provide the requested Spark execution model. <<4>> mistakes schema discovery for transformation: a crawler does not sanitize object contents.

Pass references, restrict staging and logs, and publish a batch manifest only after all expected sanitized objects pass validation. The runtime is a workload assumption, not a claim that Glue always finishes within that duration. Test capacity, schema changes and failure recovery against the target.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/author-job-glue.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html

diagram_alt: Schema metadata supports transformation, but downstream visibility requires successful sanitization and batch validation.

sources.supports: Crawlers populate catalog metadata while ETL jobs read, transform and write the underlying data.
Glue jobs can run supplied PySpark scripts on the managed Spark ETL engine.
Standard Lambda functions have a maximum configurable timeout of 900 seconds.

editorial_notes: Kept the deliberate batch runtime/reuse constraints and made complete-batch publication explicit rather than implying the service itself guarantees sanitization.
